Class Syslog

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.hardware.net.udp.Syslog
public final class Syslog extends Object
Sends log lines as RFC 5424 syslog datagrams over UDP (RFC 5426), so a board can be followed over Wi-Fi without a USB cable; juno:monitor -Djuno.syslog=<port> receives them. Each message is one datagram: <PRI>1 - HOSTNAME APP-NAME - - - MSG, with facility local0 and the nil timestamp, since a board need not know the time; the receiver stamps the arrival.

Create it once, at startup, and reuse it: it formats every message into the caller-owned buffer and sends it with one DatagramPacket, so logging in a loop allocates nothing. A whole line is info(String) and its siblings; a line built from fields uses begin(int), text(String), number(int) and send(), without String concatenation: 

syslog.begin(Syslog.INFO).text("left=").number(left).text(" right=").number(right).send();

It sends on a DatagramSocket the program owns, because a program has a single UDP socket on the board: a second socket would replace the first. The destination may be a computer's address or the broadcast address 255.255.255.255, which reaches every monitor on the local network without configuring one. A message longer than the buffer is truncated, and a failed send is counted in failures() rather than thrown, so logging never breaks the program's control loop. Characters outside printable ASCII are sent as ?.

  • Constructor Details

    • Syslog

      public Syslog(DatagramSocket socket, InetAddress destination, int port, String hostName, String appName, byte[] buffer)
      A logger sending to destination:port on socket. hostName and appName identify the sender in every frame: printable ASCII without spaces, at most 255 and 48 characters. buffer holds one frame and sets the longest message; 128 bytes suits a short trace line.
